facts.meaning: Whether a component produced at least one solid.
Whether OpenCascade's own shape-validity check (BRepCheck_Analyzer) reports no defects.
Number of top-level solids in a shape.
Solid volume of a component or assembly.
Axis-aligned bounding box (min/max/size/center per axis).
Number of named components in the assembly.
Whether two components have a real geometric intersection (INTERSECTS/TOUCHES/NO_INTERSECTION/UNKNOWN).
Volume of the boolean-common solid between two components.
Minimum distance between two components.
A group of production components forming one connected group.
A group of production components NOT connected to the rest of the production assembly.
Whether a specific required component exists in the model.
Requested vs. actually generated prong count.
Whether the StoneReference solid remains distinct from (never fused into) production metal.
Whether a fuse/cut/common boolean operation produced a real, non-empty result.
Whether a geometry builder fell back from its primary operation (e.g. band fillet, metal fuse) to a simpler alternative.
The stone reference's requested major horizontal dimension (LENGTH), taken from the component's own build-time metadata. CONSTRUCTION_PARAMETER, not an independent re-measurement.
The stone reference's measured major horizontal extent, from the independently computed axis-aligned bounding box (sizeY). Isolates LENGTH exactly only at stone.orientation == 0.
The stone reference's requested minor horizontal dimension (WIDTH), from build-time metadata. CONSTRUCTION_PARAMETER.
The stone reference's measured minor horizontal extent, from the bounding box (sizeX). Isolates WIDTH exactly only at stone.orientation == 0.
The stone reference's requested vertical dimension (DEPTH), from build-time metadata. CONSTRUCTION_PARAMETER.
The stone reference's measured vertical extent, from the bounding box (sizeZ).
The Setting family that was generated (prong/bezel).
The recorded Stone x Setting compatibility for this combination (SUPPORTED_SOFTWARE/EXPERIMENTAL/UNSUPPORTED). A recorded capability fact, never a professional judgement.
Number of components the Setting generated.
Prong count requested. Prong family only.
Prong count actually generated. Prong family only.
Which placement strategy produced the prong positions (RADIAL/OUTLINE_CARDINAL). Prong family only.
Which geometry the bezel path was derived from. Bezel family only.
Whether the bezel wall is exactly one closed solid. A topological fact only, never a claim about professional stone coverage. Bezel family only.
Which StoneSourceMode produced this stone: PARAMETRIC_REFERENCE, CUSTOM_OUTLINE, MEASURED or IMPORTED_CAD. An identity fact, never a judgement about which source is preferable.
The canonical shape (cut) identity the stone was built as. This is a CUT, never a gem species: 'emerald' here means the clipped-corner outline.
The 3D reference profile applied to the outline: FACETED_REFERENCE, CABOCHON_REFERENCE or SPHERICAL_REFERENCE. Independent of shape.
The geometry-reuse family the shape belongs to (RECTILINEAR, POLYGONAL, SPECIAL_OUTLINE, ...). A construction grouping, not a jewelry taxonomy.

How the outline behaves under reflection: RADIAL, BILATERAL_BOTH_AXES, BILATERAL_ONE_AXIS, ASYMMETRIC or UNKNOWN. Consumed by Setting to choose a placement strategy from geometry rather than from a shape name.
How the geometry is represented: PARAMETRIC, BREP_SOLID or MESH. A mesh genuinely supports fewer operations than a B-Rep solid, and this records which one a caller has.
Where the stone's dimensions came from: REQUESTED_PARAMETER, INPUT_MEASUREMENT, GENERATED_REFERENCE_MEASUREMENT, IMPORTED_GEOMETRY_MEASUREMENT or DERIVED_FROM_OUTLINE.

For a measured stone, whether its reference geometry is a MEASURED_DIMENSION_REFERENCE (an approximation built from length/width/depth) or a MEASURED_OUTLINE_REFERENCE (built from a supplied measured outline). NOT_APPLICABLE for every other source.
Whether a normalized girdle outline exists for this stone. False for the spherical reference, which genuinely has no planar girdle; never a fabricated outline.
How many ordered points the normalized outline contains. A polygonal outline reports its exact vertex count; a curved one reports its sampling resolution.
How many deterministic named anchors were derived from the outline. Anchors are geometric facts about where a feature is, never prong positions.
The rotation applied about the stone's own local vertical axis, in degrees.
Version of the reference-geometry construction that built this stone. Changes when the construction changes, so a Golden diff can be traced to a deliberate version bump.
Version of the import-normalization pipeline, for an imported stone. NOT_APPLICABLE for every other source.
Content hash of the external asset an imported stone came from. A content hash, never a filesystem path.
How many normalization operations were applied (unit conversion, winding reversal, recentring, profile defaulting). Zero means none were needed, never that normalization was skipped.
Whether the stone reference is classified as production metal. Structurally always false (LAW-006); recorded as a fact so a regression would be observable rather than silent.

notes: No fact type in this registry encodes a professional or manufacturing threshold — every 'meaning' describes a geometric measurement or a structural presence/absence check only.

forgeConsumptionStatus is 'not_consumed' for every fact as of Sprint 14: Forge's real rule engine (backend/jewelmind/validation/engine.py) does not yet read GeometricFact objects — see docs/bible/16-geometry-inspection/487-forge-fact-contract.md for the kernel-neutral contract this registry establishes for a future integration, and 494-current-runtime-inspection-gap-analysis.md for why the wiring itself was not done this Sprint (a deliberate, documented scope boundary, not an oversight).

The 6 STONE_REQUESTED_*/STONE_MEASURED_* facts (Sprint 18) deliberately pair a CONSTRUCTION_PARAMETER with an independently MEASURED_GEOMETRY counterpart so an accidental scaling or shape regression is observable as a divergence between them — compared with a software geometry tolerance, never a professional or manufacturing tolerance. See docs/bible/20-stone/574-stone-inspection-contract.md.

STONE_MEASURED_LENGTH/WIDTH derive from an axis-aligned bounding box, so they isolate LENGTH from WIDTH exactly only at stone.orientation == 0. This is a real, documented limitation of the current measurement, not an assumed exactness for every orientation.

The 8 SETTING_*/BEZEL_* facts (Sprint 19) report what the Setting System built and which recorded compatibility status applies. SETTING_COMPATIBILITY_STATUS and BEZEL_WALL_CONTINUOUS are deliberately NOT quality judgements: the first echoes the capability registry, the second is pure topology. Professional interpretation belongs to Forge/Professional Validation (SETTING-GOV-016). Prong-only facts are emitted only for the prong family and bezel-only facts only for bezel, so a fact's presence is itself honest about what was generated.
